newsitem.title: PERU: Peru reports August inflation 0.92 percent.
newsitem.headline: Peru reports August inflation 0.92 percent.

text.p: Peru's consumer prices rose 0.92 percent in August, compared with a 1.04 percent rise in the same month last year and 1.37 percent in July, government official newspaper El Peruano reported Monday.
Accumulated inflation in the first eight months of 1996 was 8.84 percent versus 7.3 percent in the same period last year, El Peruano said.

While the government and International Monetary Fund (IMF) have agreed an accumulated inflation goal for the year of between 9.5 percent and 11.5 percent, President Alberto Fujimori said Friday he expected the figure to hit 12 percent.
Peru's accumulated inflation last year fell to 10.2 percent, down from 15.4 percent the year before. The 1995 figure was the country's lowest in 23 years.
